name: claude-session-notify
description: Know the moment a Claude Code session finishes or needs you, and get back to it in one click. Run several sessions at once and keep them all under control.

commands.title: Show notifications while sharing the screen
Add hooks to Claude Code settings
Remove hooks from Claude Code settings

walkthroughs.title: Set up Notify for Claude Code
walkthroughs.description: Get notified on time and keep every Claude Code session under control.

steps.title: Connect to Claude Code
steps.description:
Claude Code tells other programs about a session only through hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json. This adds four; nothing else in the file changes. Every session reports from its next message, open ones too, and you are told when the first one does. With the claude-notify plugin for Claude Code installed, its hooks already do this and the step is done.
[Connect](command:claudeNotify.addHooks)

steps.title: Allow notifications
steps.description:
macOS asks once whether Notify for Claude Code may show notifications. Choose Allow.
[Allow notifications](command:claudeNotify.allowNotifications)

steps.title: Keep them on screen
steps.description:
Optional. With the Persistent style a notification stays until you deal with it, instead of sliding away after a few seconds.
[Open notification settings](command:claudeNotify.openNotificationSettings)

steps.title: Show them while sharing the screen
steps.description:
Optional. While your screen is shared or recorded — a call, a demo — macOS hides every notification. Under Allow notifications, turn on When mirroring or sharing the display.
[Open notification settings](command:claudeNotify.showWhileSharing)

steps.title: Try it
steps.description:
Give Claude something that takes longer than 45 seconds, in any session, and switch to another app. A shorter turn finishes quietly — you were watching it.
[Send a test notification](command:claudeNotify.test)
[Choose how long a turn must last](command:claudeNotify.chooseQuietTime)

claudeNotify.enabled.description: Announce sessions that finish or start waiting for you.

enumDescriptions: Turns long enough to look away from. The default.
Only the long ones — for those who dislike being interrupted.
claudeNotify.minTurnSeconds.description: Announce a finished turn only when it took longer than this. A shorter one finishes quietly — you were watching it. Longer means fewer notifications.

claudeNotify.events.description: Which events are worth a notification.

claudeNotify.style.description: Linux and Windows only. On macOS how long a notification stays is set in System Settings → Notifications → terminal-notifier (Persistent keeps it until you act).

claudeNotify.sound.description: Play a sound with the notification.

claudeNotify.editorNotifications.description: Also show each notification inside the VS Code window that holds the session, with a button that opens it.

claudeNotify.statusBar.description: Show running and waiting sessions in the status bar.
